headline: Elon Musk has answered the Broadcom chief executive's warning about reckless AI investing with the line "No crying in the casino".
score_reason: Pool 8 lowered by 2: a one-line quip about remarks made on 12 Oct, before the window, with no new facts, and the Barron's text could not be read.
importance_line: Musk's quip adds attention but no evidence to the debate over whether AI spending has run ahead of returns, which matters first to people whose savings are in AI-heavy shares, then to lenders, then to the companies, but the reply is only a quip with no argument or figures behind it.
summary: Barron's reports that Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, answered "No crying in the casino" after Hock Tan, chief executive of the US chip maker Broadcom, told an event in Singapore on Monday 12 Oct that many AI investors "have no clue" what they are putting money into and are in something "almost like" a casino, as Benzinga, on Yahoo Finance, quotes Bloomberg's account. This continues the story our 12 Oct 2026 edition carried from Reuters, in which Tan said money, not chips or memory, will be Broadcom's biggest limit; what is new today is Musk's reply.
notes: Barron's text blocked (401). Tan's remarks read on Yahoo Finance (Benzinga, https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/broadcom-ceo-says-many-ai-193518585.html); Musk's quote read on ABAB News (https://www.ababnews.com/news/0825a742-029b-4069-83f6-00458b5570dc) and in the Barron's and Benzinga headlines. Musk's post itself was not opened.
